title: XVII-XXIX: secondary affections — desire, abomination, joy, grief, hope, fear, wrath
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Wrath stands as ye affection belonging toward driving away by means belonging toward that same which God wills to punish ye sinning creature. XXIX. Fear stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God declines evil as a possible future. XXVIII. Confidence stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God with great spirit pursues ye desired good. XXVII. Hope stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God pursues ye best good. XXV. Grief stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God holds Himself toward ye sense belonging toward present evil. XXII. Joy stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God delights in a good thing as present plus agreeing with Himself plus His will. XXI. works belonging toward impiety plus iniquity, plus omission belonging toward remuneration — abomination stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God execrates things abhorrent out from His nature — unbelief. XX. Desire stands as as it were Gods affection belonging toward obtaining things agreeing with His nature — faith plus works belonging toward piety plus justice prescribed by means belonging toward Himself to intelligent creatures plus performable through His grace. XIX. then joy plus grief — in ye concupiscible first stands as desire plus abomination. XVIII. that same which stand as occupied not about good plus evil commonly, but in species about that same as present or absent, plus stand as distinguished out from ye mode belonging toward our consideration inasmuch as they stand as conceived either in ye concupiscible or in ye irascible — there follow attributes analogous to affections as it were arising out from ye primary. And these things concerning Gods attributes that same which have analogy with affections as it were primary: XVII.
pass_b_english: XVII. And these things concerning Gods attributes which have analogy with affections as it were primary: there follow attributes analogous to affections as it were arising from the primary, which are occupied not about good and evil commonly, but in species about that as present or absent, and are distinguished from the mode of our consideration inasmuch as they are conceived either in the concupiscible or in the irascible.

XVIII. In the concupiscible first is desire and abomination, then joy and grief. XIX. Desire is as it were Gods affection of obtaining things agreeing with His nature — faith and works of piety and justice prescribed by Himself to intelligent creatures and performable through His grace. XX. Abomination is that by which God execrates things abhorrent from His nature — unbelief, works of impiety and iniquity, and omission of remuneration.

XXI. Joy is that by which God delights in a good thing as present and agreeing with Himself and His will. XXII. Grief is that by which God holds Himself toward the sense of present evil. XXV. Hope is that by which God pursues the best good. XXVII. Confidence is that by which God with great spirit pursues the desired good. XXVIII. Fear is that by which God declines evil as a possible future. XXIX. Wrath is the affection of driving away by which God wills to punish the sinning creature.
source_text: XVII. Atque haec de attributis Dei quae analogiam habent cum affectibus quasi primis: sequuntur attributa quae analoga sunt affectibus quasi ortis a primis, qui non circa bonum et malum communiter, sed in specie circa illud qua praesens aut absens est occupantur, et distinguuntur e nostra considerationis modo, quatenus vel in concupiscibili vel in irascibili concipiuntur. XVIII. In concupiscibili primo est desiderium et abominatio, deinde gaudium et dolor. XIX. Desiderium est quasi affectus Dei res naturae suae convenientes, fidem et opera pietatis atque justitiae creaturis intelligentibus a se praescripta et per gratiam suam praestabilia, obtinendi. XX. Abominatio est, qua Deus res a natura sua abhorrentes, infidelitatem, opera impietatis et iniquitatis, omissionemque remunerationis, exsecratur. XXI. Gaudium est, quo Deus in re bona tanquam praesente et sibi voluntatique suae congruente delectatur. XXII. Dolor est, quo Deus se habet ad sensum mali praesentis. XXV. Spes est, qua Deus bonum opimum prosequitur. XXVII. Confidentia est, qua Deus ingenti spiritu bonum desideratum persequitur. XXVIII. Metus est, quo Deus malum, ut futurum possibile, declinat. XXIX. Ira est affectus depulsionis, quo Deus creaturam peccantem punire vult — Psal.; Deut.; Ezech.
